21	
22	## Opening Settings
23	
24	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.
25	
26	The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.
27	
28	Closing it loses nothing, because every control saves as you use it, or when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.
29	
30	Two other places send you here:
31	
32	- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
33	- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note under the button in the Generate Captions sheet, and the button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you.
34	
35	[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.
36	
37	## The info buttons
38	
39	The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.
40	
41	- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
42	- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.
43	
44	VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.
45	
46	## MCP
47	
48	This section tells an MCP client, such as Claude Code, how to reach Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.
49	
50	Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.
51	
52	**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:
53	
54	```sh
55	claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
56	```
57	
58	The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."
59	
60	The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
61	
62	The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
63	
64	## Assistant
65	
66	This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
67	
68	| Control | What it does | Default |
69	| --- | --- | --- |
70	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
71	| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
72	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
73	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
74	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
75	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
76	
77	There's no **Verify** button here, because Frame Job doesn't call Anthropic itself. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.
78	
79	**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.
80	
81	**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
82	
83	Earlier renders don't survive compaction, and each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
84	
85	Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
86	
87	The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.
88	
89	## Transcription
90	
91	This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
92	
93	| Control | What it does | Default |
94	| --- | --- | --- |
95	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
96	| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
97	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
98	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
99	| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
100	| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |
101	
102	A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses.
103	
104	**Verify** checks the key a real run would use: one you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:
105	
106	| The line says | What it means |
107	| --- | --- |
108	| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
109	| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
110	| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
111	| AssemblyAI's own message | The check failed, and the message says why. |
112	
113	Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.
114	
115	The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
116	
117	## Playback
118	
119	This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.
120	
121	| Control | What it does | Default |
122	| --- | --- | --- |
123	| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
124	| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |
125	
126	Both save the moment you change them. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
127	
128	Anything you do in Frame Job stops the pass at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.
129	
130	It never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
131	
132	## How the key fields behave
133	
134	The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.
135	
136	- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
137	- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".
138	
139	The line under the controls reports what happened:
140	
141	| The line says | What it means |
142	| --- | --- |
143	| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
144	| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
145	| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |
146	
147	[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.
148	
149	## Agents and Settings
150	
151	No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.
152	
153	An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered without a key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
154	
155	## Related
156	
157	- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
158	- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)
159	- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
160

1	---
2	title: "What Frame Job remembers"
3	description: "Which view choices, pane sizes, sheets and panels reopen the way you left them, what starts fresh in each window, and where those choices are kept."
4	---
5	
6	Frame Job remembers some of your choices between launches, so the next window or sheet opens the way you left it. These are your choices on this Mac, not part of a project, so none of them travels with a `.framejob` package. The [Settings](/reference/settings/) window has its own page.
7	
8	## View choices
9	
10	The last choice you made, in any window, is what the next window opens with. These apply to every project.
11	
12	| Choice | Where | Options | Default |
13	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
14	| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, <kbd>N</kbd>, or **Snap** in the timeline bar | On, off | On |
15	| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or **Safe** in the toolbar | On, off | Off |
16	| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>), which reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown, hidden | Shown |
17	| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or **S**, **M** and **L** in the timeline bar | Small, Medium, Large | Medium |
18	| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full, Half, Quarter | Full |
19	
20	Preview quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/).
21	
22	Holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that's remembered.
23	
24	## Pane sizes
25	
26	Drag the divider above the timeline, or the one left of the inspector, and new windows open at that size.
27	
28	| Pane | Range | Default |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| Inspector width | 280 to 440 pt | 304 pt |
31	| Timeline height | 140 pt to 60% of the window | 300 pt |
32	
33	The canvas stays at least 380 pt wide, and the area above the timeline at least 220 pt tall.
34	
35	Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, or hiding and showing the inspector, changes nothing that's remembered, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.
36	
37	## Preview Window frame
38	
39	**View ▸ Preview Window** (<kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>) opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. There's one saved frame for every project.
40	
41	With two projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved. Whether the window is open isn't remembered. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
42	
43	## Sheets
44	
45	These reopen on what you chose last time. Any sheet not listed here opens on its defaults every time.
46	
47	| Where | What's remembered | When it's saved |
48	| --- | --- | --- |
49	| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | **Engine:** (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), **Style:**, and the **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses** boxes | As you change each one |
50	| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with, except **Dynamic Range** | When you press **Export…** or **Add to Queue** |
51	| **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** | When you press **Zoom** |
52	| **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:** | When you press **Follow** |
53	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:**, shared with Follow Subject | When you press **Make** |
54	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | **Rate:**, **Shortest stretch:** and **Keep pitch** | When you press **Apply** |
55	| **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** | **Minimum shot:**, **Cut:**, **Crosstalk:** and **Ignore bleed:** | When you press **Switch** |
56	| The **Normalize** row of the [Volume section](/audio/normalize/) | Its mode, **Peak** or **Loudness**, and its target in LUFS | As you change each one |
57	| The Document tab's **Canvas** section | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with your next [canvas-size](/projects/canvas-size/) change | As you tick it |
58	
59	Where a choice is saved on a press, cancelling the sheet saves nothing.
60	
61	The first time you export, the sheet opens on H.264 at document size. Named export presets are kept in a file, so they're on [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).
62	
63	**Follow:** can read differently in the two sheets that share it. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, it opens on **Speaker** again, and Follow Subject, which has no such choice, opens on **Subject**.
64	
65	**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference, not an edit, so undo doesn't reach it.
66	
67	No agent tool reads any of these. An agent's call always names its own values.
68	
69	## Recorder panel
70	
71	**File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) reopens on your last choices, each saved as you change it.
72	
73	| Group | What's remembered |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| Source | The display in **Source:**, **Include Frame Job windows** |
76	| Camera | **Camera:** and **Format:**, **Record the camera too**, **Layout:**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands** |
77	| Sound | **Microphone:**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **System Audio:** |
78	| Pointer and keys | **Cursor:**, **Show Clicks:**, **Record shortcuts** |
79	| When it lands | **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts**, **Speed up typing** |
80	| Picture | **Rate:**, **Size:** |
81	
82	Until you change them, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are off, **Zoom in on clicks** and **Show shortcuts** are on, **Layout:** is **Corner**, and **Cursor:** follows the default for the source.
83	
84	A few things don't last between launches:
85	
86	- **Record Into:** is never remembered.
87	- A picked window, **Microphone Only** and **Camera** as the **Source:** row last for the session only. The camera you chose is remembered, even though the row isn't.
88	
89	See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
90	
91	## Inspector sections
92	
93	Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, section by section, in every window. Only a click on a section's header is remembered.
94	
95	A section you've never clicked opens in its default state. Transform, a text or shape's main section, a graphic's Properties, and the sections of the Media and Document tabs start open, and most others start closed. If that would leave a Clip tab with every section shut, the first one you've never clicked opens. See [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).
96	
97	## Permission questions
98	
99	macOS shows its Screen Recording prompt only once, so Frame Job remembers that it has already asked. A later press of **Record** without the permission opens the Screen Recording pane of System Settings instead of the prompt. Input Monitoring, which **Record shortcuts** needs, is remembered the same way. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
100	
101	## Convert on import
102	
103	When macOS can't open a file and Frame Job offers to repackage or convert it, ticking **Do this automatically from now on** in that alert remembers your answer:
104	
105	- Ticked with **Convert** or **Repackage**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
106	- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails.
107	
108	There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
109	
110	```sh
111	defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
112	```
113	
114	See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
115	
116	## Update checks
117	
118	The downloaded copy of Frame Job remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).
119	
120	## What is not remembered
121	
122	**View ▸ Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** all start off in each new window. None of them changes an export.
123	
124	Nothing about the scopes is kept: a new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. The Loudness Meter starts off and empty.
125	
126	Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead, the selection and the in/out range aren't remembered between launches.
127	
128	Some rows in the sheets above are never remembered, even though the rows around them are:
129	
130	- **Zoom:** in Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version
131	- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
132	- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
133	- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
134	- **Dynamic Range** in Export
135	- Every choice in **Match Audio…**
136	
137	## Where these are kept
138	
139	All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.
140	
141	## Related
142	
143	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
144	- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
145	- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,

  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the

  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op

- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

content.content:
Settings is one window, not a set of tabs. It holds four sections, top to
bottom: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. On a
short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls. Closing it
loses nothing: every control saves as you use it, or when you press its
**Save** button, as described below. While it is open it is listed in the
**Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ button.
Rest the pointer on it for a moment to see that section's explanation; click
it to keep the explanation open, and click it again (or anywhere else, or
press Escape) to close it.

*Agents:* no MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Keys, the model,
the region and Background render are set only by a person in this window.
An agent's cloud tools (`transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine,
`transcribe_for_fillers`) do use the key and region saved here, so a person
must set the key first; without one they refuse, at the point they would
send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸
Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use is answered
without a key. The assistant's own tool, `assistant_send` (a dev tool), refuses
the same way with the Anthropic sentence.

## MCP
| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard (assemblyai.com/dashboard) in your browser, where you get a key and see what you have spent. | — |

The key field behaves exactly like the Assistant's: a fixed row of dots when
a key is stored, "Paste your key" when one is not, and "Key saved.",
"Key removed." or "No API key is set." on the line beneath, and "The API key
could not be saved: <reason>" if the key file cannot be written or removed.

A transcript made in one region cannot be seen from the other, so the region
is a choice you make, not a fallback. Pick the region your AssemblyAI account
uses.

### Verify

**Verify** checks whichever key a real run would use: the one typed in the
field if you have typed one and not saved it yet, otherwise the stored key,
otherwise the key in the environment (see below). It is disabled when there
is no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.

| Line under the controls | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Checking… | The request is in flight. |
| Key accepted | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
| Settings changed since this check began. Verify again. | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| An AssemblyAI message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed; the text says why. |

Saving, removing or changing the region also tells an open Generate Captions
sheet straight away, so it can enable its button without being reopened.

### What the ⓘ says

The Transcription ⓘ explains what leaves your Mac: with AssemblyAI chosen,
the audio of the files you are captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back
and then deleted from AssemblyAI. Frame Job asks for the delete as soon as it
has the words, and retries it at the start of the next run if it did not go
through. Nothing is uploaded until you press Generate, and captions made on
your Mac never leave it. It also gives AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame
